evidence.quote: extract the closed history into a flat, self-describing archive — the records plus a schema description plus a document explaining what the fields mean

observations.why: Translates technical architectural architecture requirements into plain-spoken concrete operational items.

evidence.quote: Not a database dump that needs the vendor's version of their engine to restore. Not a proprietary export format. Flat files, an open format, a schema next to them

observations.why: Deliberate demystification of technical system preservation into transparent, accessible terminology.

evidence.quote: The data is easy to keep. The meaning is what rots.

observations.why: Aphoristic maxim distilling a complex archival principle into stark, plain language.

evidence.quote: So the position is: the legacy platform is switched off when the last site goes live, the closed history is extracted first into an open self-describing archive, and the retention period comes from legal in writing before we sign anything with the vendor about decommissioning.

observations.why: Formally crystallizing meeting consensus into an explicit governance position.
